Subject: Performance MAP kickoff + clarifying throughput targets

Jasmine / team — thanks again for last week's demo. As discussed, Acme is looking to validate Redwood's serving profile against our production workload before committing to Dedicated.

High-level asks for the POC:
- Throughput target: sustain 400 QPS with 512-token average request size (target sustained for 30 min).
- Latency: p50 < 45ms, p95 < 220ms for our typical prompt mix.
- TTFT: as low as possible; call out cold vs warm TTFT.
- Concurrency: support ~80 concurrent sessions during highest load.
- Unit economics: provide estimated $/1M tokens and tokens/sec per USD based on the setup you'd recommend.

Can you put together a MAP + evaluation plan with milestones and acceptance criteria? We need a go/no-go decision by 2026-05-02 to hit our Q2 roadmap.

Also please send any instrumentation/agent we should run on our side to collect token distribution.

Thanks,
Ellen
Product Owner — Acme Analytics

Ellen — appreciate the clear targets. Draft MAP and evaluation plan attached (MAP_milestones_v1.xlsx) and a first-pass throughput report (acme_throughput_report_v1.csv). Summary below.

Quick summary / plan:
1) Goals and acceptance criteria (POC success = all must pass):
   - Sustained throughput: 400 QPS sustained for 30m with 512-token avg => measured sustained QPS >= 380 (we allow a 5% margin).
   - Latency: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 220ms.
   - TTFT: warm TTFT <= 18ms; cold TTFT recorded separately.
   - Concurrency: handle 80 concurrent sessions with <5% error rate.
   - Economics: provide a unit-econ summary; target cost < $X per 1M tokens (see breakdown below).

2) Benchmarks we'll run (timeline in MAP):
   - Day 1 (2026-04-15): Baseline single-model latency profile (p50/p95/TTFT).
   - Day 2 (2026-04-16): Batching & KV-cache enabled, measure tokens/sec and sustained QPS at incremental concurrency levels (10,25,50,80).
   - Day 3 (2026-04-17): Long-run 30-minute sustained QPS test at target concurrency + failover/fallback verification.
   - Day 4 (2026-04-18): Economics report + handoff + joint review.

3) Acceptance instrumentation: Redwood will provide a lightweight agent and a prometheus export map; we ask Acme to run the collector (instructions in the Drive link).

4) Unit economics approach (preview):
   - Measured tokens/sec (sustained) — benchmarked under chosen quantization / instance type.
   - GPU effective hour cost (cloud instance amortized + infra) => used to compute $/1M tokens.
   - We will present a tokens/sec per dollar metric to make tradeoffs explicit.

Initial numbers from our lab run (attached CSV shows raw samples):
- Model variant: redwood-legacy-3B-int8 (proxy for your workload)
- Sustained tokens/sec (single GPU, optimized batching, warm): 24,800 tokens/sec
- Equivalent sustained QPS with 512-token avg: ~48 QPS per GPU (24,800 / 512)
- To reach 400 QPS (target) estimated GPUs required: 9 GPUs (with 10% headroom)
- Cost assumptions: $3.25 per GPU-hour (amortized infra) => estimated token cost: ~ $0.16 per 1k tokens => ~$160 per 1M tokens (detailed sheet attached)

Notes: these are conservative early numbers; Day 2/3 will produce POC-validated figures. Marcus will run the long-run test and finalize the econ tab.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
- 2026-04-15: Baseline results (internal)
- 2026-04-16: Joint load tests (engineering sync)
- 2026-04-17: Long-run stress + resiliency tests
- 2026-04-18: Final economics and sign-off
- 2026-05-02: Go/no-go decision (Acme execs)

Next steps: Marcus will kick off the load harness on Friday. Aditya, can you confirm the instance sizing and quantization you recommend for the POC?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff + clarifying throughput targets — final POC results + econ summary

Ellen / team — thanks for the session and the patience. We completed the MAP tests and consolidated the results below (full CSV attached). Key takeaways and acceptance mapping are at the top.

POC acceptance mapping (all criteria met except noted):
- Sustained throughput: Target 400 QPS for 30m. Observed sustained median = 392 QPS (30m window), peak 410 QPS. Status: PASS (within 2% margin).
- Latency: p50 = 42ms, p95 = 210ms. Status: PASS.
- TTFT: warm TTFT = 16.3ms, cold TTFT (first start) = 112ms. Status: PASS for warm; cold recorded for baseline.
- Concurrency: 80 concurrent sessions simulated; error rate 1.8% (background retries reduced impact). Status: PASS (<=5% error).
- Resiliency: fallback to redwood-legacy-1.5B when queue depth exceeded; fallback latency p95 = 360ms. Status: PASS (fallback verified).

Throughput & unit economics (finalized numbers):
- Model variant: redwood-legacy-3B-int8 (primary); fallback redwood-legacy-1.5B-int8
- Sustained tokens/sec (warm, optimized batching): 25,200 tokens/sec per optimized GPU
- Sustained QPS per GPU (512-token avg): ~49.2 QPS
- GPUs to support 400 QPS: 9 GPUs (8.13 raw -> rounded to 9 for headroom and scheduling)
- Measured tokens per GPU-hour (sustained): 25,200 * 3600 = 90,720,000 tokens/hr
- Cost assumptions (POC environment, amortized): $3.10 per GPU-hour (spot-amortized rate + infra)
- Cost per 1M tokens: (3.10 / 90.72) ≈ $0.0342 per 1k tokens => ~$34.2 per 1M tokens (POC config)
- Tokens/sec per USD (sustained): 25,200 tokens/sec / (3.10/3600) USD/sec => simplified metric: ~8,132,000 tokens per USD-hour equivalent (see attached econ tab).

Sensitivity (int8 vs int4, same infra):
- int4 preliminary (experimental): tokens/sec per GPU +18% => ~29,736 tokens/sec; model quality regression within acceptable thresholds on our eval set for your prompts. If int4 is acceptable, GPUs required drop to 7 (with same headroom) and cost per 1M tokens falls to ~$27.6. We flagged this as optional in the MAP.

MAP Milestones (finalized):
- 2026-04-15: Baseline - COMPLETE
- 2026-04-16: Joint load tests - COMPLETE (09:00-12:30 PT joint window)
- 2026-04-17: Long-run stability - COMPLETE
- 2026-04-18: Final econ & review - COMPLETE
- 2026-05-02: Executive sign-off decision (schedule maintained)

Attachments: acme_throughput_report_v1.csv (raw logs), MAP_milestones_v1.xlsx (signed snapshot)

Recommended next steps:
1) If Acme accepts int8 baseline, we can publish a draft Dedicated sizing quote (9 GPUs / N hours) and expected monthly cost bucket.
2) If Acme is comfortable testing int4, we can run a 24-hour int4 soak test and validate quality metrics across your exact eval set.
3) Schedule an exec review with cost summary week of 2026-04-27 to prepare for the 05-02 decision.

Ellen — happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk the econ numbers.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
